summary:
The Coxmox is an innovative educational project that transforms real-world Earth events into an accessible audio experience using NASA's open data. Its main concept is simple: “See Earth change. Hear Earth change.” The project aims to make Earth science more inclusive, especially for blind and low-vision individuals, by combining an interactive map with instrumental music and a speaking agent.

The system uses NASA EONET event data, NASA GIBS map imagery, and NOAA ONI climate information. Users can explore global environmental events, filter them by category, and select individual events. It offers two listening modes: Instrumental Mode and Vocal Mode. In Instrumental Mode, each event category is represented by a unique musical instrument. For example, wildfires use marimba, earthquakes use timpani, and volcanoes use pipe organ. Event magnitude slightly influences pitch and playback speed. Vocal Mode uses browser speech technology to explain event details in simple language.

The project is developed using Vite, JavaScript, Leaflet, browser audio, and speech technologies. It also supports keyboard navigation, screen-reader announcements, reduced motion, and optional location sharing.

Overall, The Coxmox combines technology, accessibility, music, and environmental awareness to create an engaging way to understand Earth's changing conditions. It is an educational prototype, not an official NASA warning or forecasting system.
details: Coxmox is the project that I am working on. We have chosen the theme earth jukebox. Coxmox will pull all data from NASA. Gather every piece of information about disasters and other app features. Coxmox will turn each disaster into a music track and a voice alert. When I open the Coxmox app Apple will automatically find the location search for disasters and send a notification with custom team music that tells me which disaster it is explains how far it is, in which direction and how big the impact will be. Coxmox also lets me search for disasters around the world using 2D and 3D map displays. Coxmox lets me pick a custom location and search, for past or predicted future disasters. All past disaster data are stored in a database and Coxmox can look up older disasters to suggest what I should do now.
